iamArtifacts.method: Only isolated STS federation sessions; credentials consumed in memory. Destination resource policy removed at sequence 283.
iamArtifacts.sharedSLR: DynamoDB automatically created its previously absent SLR on first enable; it was preserved, never modified or deleted by this probe.

limitations: Kinesis/DynamoDB data-event CloudTrail logging was not enabled account-wide or on any trail. Owned-resource management-event history was queried only; caller-versus-SLR identity is supported by isolated-session behavior and read-only role policy, not an assumed PutRecords CloudTrail event.
TTL, stream encryption/KMS failures and long outage retry exhaustion were not induced by this tiny resource experiment.
Initial invalid ARN probes overlapped asynchronous state; isolated-enable labels repeat account/region/resource-type admission after observing DISABLED.

Owned-resource CloudTrail lookups returned CreateTable/CreateStream/DescribeTable events but no targeted streaming-destination events within the observation window; their CloudTrail envelopes are not inferred.

claims: caller enable permission documented with kinesis:PutRecords and ListStreams; examples differ

experimentNotes: Initial admission sequence accepted nonexistent and wrong-service stream ARNs asynchronously. Continuation reuses exactly the same owned table and stream and retains initial calls; initial expectation failure was experimental, not an AWS error.

Initial admission sequence accepted nonexistent and wrong-service stream ARNs asynchronously. Continuation reuses exactly the same owned table and stream and retains initial calls; initial expectation failure was experimental, not an AWS error.

The deliberately overlapping Enable following Disable succeeded after the rapid native disable completed; it reactivated the destination. The experiment replaced its now-inapplicable DISABLED waiter with an explicit second disable and continued using the same original resources.

analysis.evidenceBasis: Derived only from retained native calls and exact destination records; finite negative observation windows are not a universal delivery guarantee.

publicStreams.observed: Table created without public StreamSpecification; destination records were delivered without enabling public DynamoDB Streams. DescribeTable did not gain public stream fields.

unchangedAndAbsentWrites.observation: Identical ordinary PutItem, UpdateItem, BatchWriteItem Put and PartiQL Update produced no additional record in the exercised windows. Identical TransactWriteItems Put and Update, and ExecuteTransaction PartiQL Update DID produce MODIFY with equal OldImage/NewImage; do not apply universal no-op suppression. Absent DeleteItem, batch/transaction deletes and PartiQL deletes produced no record in these windows.

callerAndServiceAuthority.observation: Explicit caller PutRecord/PutRecords session denial was verified directly. Enable can admit ENABLING before asynchronous permission failure. After privileged enable, table writes under the same caller denial delivered records; SLR trust/policy identify service-owned destination write authority.
callerAndServiceAuthority.recoveryObservation: No slr-denied record arrived during the scoped resource-policy denial window. After policy removal, recovery-barrier arrived before the older slr-denied item, directly observing delayed retry recovery and cross-item out-of-order delivery. Destination remained ACTIVE.

timestampPrecision.observation: MILLISECOND records contain integer epoch milliseconds and omit ApproximateCreationDateTimePrecision; MICROSECOND records contain integer epoch microseconds and an explicit MICROSECOND field. Exact values are retained in recordReferencesByItemKey.

envelope.observation: Destination JSON is not a copied DynamoDB Streams GetRecords envelope; it carries tableName and recordFormat, lacks a DynamoDB stream SequenceNumber, and uses Kinesis SequenceNumber externally.

recordSize.observed: For transaction key pk=transaction and n=1, INSERT SizeBytes=29; equal-image MODIFY SizeBytes=45. These equal Keys+NewImage and Keys+OldImage+NewImage respectively, not max(old,new).

disableOverlapAndDuplicateDelivery.observation: A write approximately two seconds after DISABLED was observed still arrived. After reenable MICROSECOND, the one reenabled-write mutation produced two INSERT records with distinct eventIDs and Kinesis sequence numbers: one MICROSECOND and one MILLISECOND. Old/new delivery-pipeline overlap is an inference; exact duplicate notifications and precision contrast are observed. Do not infer instantaneous cutoff from the status alone.

cloudTrail.scope: Only the owned unique table/stream name and owned table ARN were queried; no account-wide or event-name lookup.
